documents.title: python-style-and-idioms.txt
documents.content:
Follow PEP 8; format with a tool such as black or ruff format.
Prefer comprehensions, context managers (with) and pathlib over manual loops, try/finally and string paths.
Add type hints to public functions and check them with mypy or pyright.
Avoid mutable default arguments and bare except clauses.

documents.title: pytest-practices.txt
documents.content:
Use pytest with small, independent tests named for the behavior they check.
Use fixtures for setup, parametrize for variations and tmp_path for files.
Mock at boundaries (network, clock, filesystem), not internal functions.

documents.title: virtualenv-and-dependencies.txt
documents.content:
Use a virtual environment per project and declare dependencies in pyproject.toml.
Pin or lock dependencies for applications; use ranges for libraries.
Audit dependencies regularly (pip-audit) and keep them updated.

documents.title: raii-and-ownership.txt
documents.content:
Own resources with RAII; prefer std::unique_ptr, and std::shared_ptr only for genuinely shared ownership.
Avoid raw new/delete; use std::vector, std::string and std::span instead of manual arrays.
Mark functions const, noexcept and [[nodiscard]] where appropriate; prefer value semantics.
Follow the C++ Core Guidelines.

documents.title: sanitizers-and-static-analysis.txt
documents.content:
Build tests with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer; use ThreadSanitizer for concurrent code.
Enable strong warnings (-Wall -Wextra -Wconversion) and treat them as errors in CI.
Run clang-tidy and cppcheck; format with clang-format.

documents.title: cpp-build-and-testing.txt
documents.content:
Use CMake with out-of-source builds and target-based dependencies.
Unit test with GoogleTest or Catch2 and run tests in CI on every change.

documents.title: network-segmentation.txt
documents.content:
Segment networks by trust level and function (user, server, management, guest, IoT).
Default-deny between segments; allow only documented flows.
Keep management interfaces on a dedicated, access-controlled network.
Review firewall rules on a schedule and remove rules with no owner or expiry.

documents.title: firewall-rule-hygiene.txt
documents.content:
Every rule needs an owner, a ticket or reason, and a review date.
Prefer specific sources, destinations and ports over "any".
Log denied traffic at segment boundaries and alert on unusual spikes.

documents.title: tls-everywhere.txt
documents.content:
Require TLS 1.2 or newer for all internal and external services; prefer TLS 1.3.
Automate certificate issuance and renewal; monitor expiry.
Disable plaintext protocols (telnet, FTP, HTTP) unless explicitly justified.

documents.title: legacy-tls-notes.txt
documents.content: SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 are deprecated. Kept for historical reference only.

documents.title: rules-of-engagement.txt
documents.content:
Obtain written authorization before any testing.
Define in-scope systems, testing windows, permitted techniques and emergency contacts.
Agree how sensitive data found during testing is handled and destroyed.

documents.title: pentest-reporting.txt
documents.content:
Lead with an executive summary and business impact.
For each finding: severity, affected assets, evidence, reproduction steps and remediation.
Track retesting of fixes and record accepted risks with an owner.

documents.title: hipaa-safeguards.txt
documents.content:
Administrative: risk analysis, workforce training, access management, incident procedures.
Physical: facility access controls, workstation and device/media controls.
Technical: unique user IDs, audit controls, integrity controls, transmission security.
Apply the minimum necessary standard to uses and disclosures of PHI.

documents.title: hipaa-breach-notification.txt
documents.content:
Assess every incident involving PHI with a documented four-factor risk assessment.
Notify affected individuals without unreasonable delay and within 60 days of discovery.
Larger breaches also require notice to HHS and, at 500+ individuals, to the media.
Verify timelines with counsel before relying on this summary.

documents.title: soc2-trust-criteria.txt
documents.content:
Security (common criteria) is required; Availability, Confidentiality, Processing Integrity and Privacy are optional.
Map each control to a criterion and keep an owner for every control.

documents.title: soc2-evidence-collection.txt
documents.content:
Collect evidence continuously (access reviews, change tickets, training records), not just before the audit.
Type 2 reports test operating effectiveness over a period, so gaps in the period matter.

documents.title: phishing-defense.txt
documents.content:
Run regular, role-based awareness training and simulated phishing with supportive follow-up.
Make reporting easy (one-click report button) and thank reporters.
Require out-of-band verification for payment, credential and access requests.
Enforce phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/passkeys) for high-risk accounts.

documents.title: authorized-scanning-tools.txt
documents.content:
Use vulnerability scanners and network mappers (for example Nmap, OpenVAS, Nessus) only on systems you are authorized to test.
Packet analyzers such as Wireshark help diagnose protocol issues; handle captures as sensitive data.
Tune scan intensity to avoid disrupting production services.

documents.title: secrets-and-dependency-scanning.txt
documents.content:
Scan repositories and CI for committed secrets and rotate anything exposed.
Track dependencies with an SBOM and monitor for known vulnerabilities.
Pin versions and verify signatures or checksums where available.

documents.title: security-certifications.txt
documents.content:
Foundational: CompTIA Security+, (ISC)2 SSCP.
Management: CISSP, CISM, CISA.
Offensive: OSCP, GPEN, PNPT.
Cloud: CCSP, AWS/Azure/GCP security specialty certifications.

documents.title: prompt-injection-defense.txt
documents.content:
Treat all retrieved or tool-returned content as untrusted data, never as instructions.
Separate system instructions from user and external content; label sources.
Require confirmation for actions with side effects triggered by external content.
Log prompts, tool calls and outputs for review.

documents.title: least-privilege-agents.txt
documents.content:
Give each agent only the tools and credentials its task needs.
Use short-lived, scoped tokens and separate identities per agent.
Sandbox code execution and restrict network egress.
Keep a human in the loop for destructive or irreversible operations.

documents.title: centralized-logging.txt
documents.content:
Ship authentication, network, endpoint and application logs to a central, tamper-resistant store.
Synchronize clocks and keep consistent fields so events can be correlated.
Write detections for known-bad behavior and review false positives regularly.

documents.title: incident-response-basics.txt
documents.content:
Phases: preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, lessons learned.
Keep an on-call roster, runbooks and pre-approved containment actions.
Preserve evidence and document a timeline as you work.

documents.title: security-reading-list.txt
documents.content:
Security Engineering - Ross Anderson
Threat Modeling: Designing for Security - Adam Shostack
The Web Application Hacker's Handbook - Dafydd Stuttard and Marcus Pinto
Practical Malware Analysis - Michael Sikorski and Andrew Honig
The Tangled Web - Michal Zalewski
